newsitem.title: FINLAND: ATHLETICS-JAVELIN DUO BACKLEY AND HATTESTAD SHINE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JAVELIN DUO BACKLEY AND HATTESTAD SHINE.

text.p: Briton Steve Backley beat Czech Olympic and world champion Jan Zelezny and Norwegian Trine Hattestad threw the women's world best this year with outstanding javelin performances on Wednesday.
Backley stunned the competiton at the Helsinki international athletics meeting with a massive 87.96 metres first-round throw.
Zelezny, his technique askew, never came close and finished fourth with 83.30.
"I am very satisfied," Backley said. "It was a good competition and a good one to win."
He said he had watched Zelzny "very carefully" and had adapted his own style slightly. "It seems to have worked. Zelezny looked tired and beating him tasted very good," he said.
Sporting her trademark sunny smile and long blonde hair, Hattestad threw 69.66 metres to win the women's event.
"I am feeling stronger with every competition," the mother of two said. "It is great to be throwing nearly 70 metres already."

The meeting also marked the return to competition of pole vault world record holder Sergei Bubka of Ukraine. He cleared only 5.60 metres to finish fifth in his first outing since an injury forced him out of the Atlanta Olympics last year.
"Basically I can say it feels okay," he said. "I am clearly not 100 percent, but I feel I am on the way back. I need to start somewhere -- I only began jogging in April."

His return took place in the stadium where he first rose to fame, winning the inaugural world championship title 14 years ago. "Helsinki marked the start of my career. I hope it will also mark the restart," Bubka said.
On the track, Mark Richardson of Britain ran the first sub-45 seconds 400 metres this season by a European, clocking 44.91.
"I have to be satisfied. I eased off on the line and that probably cost me a couple of hundredths," Richardson said.
The men's 100 metres race lost some of its sparkle before the start with Britain's Linford Christie wihdrawing with a nagging knee injury.
Frankie Fredericks of Namibia cruised to victory in 10.05 seconds -- a personal best this season.
Fredericks beat American Tim Montgomery, still suffering from jet-lag after finishing second over 100 metres in the U.S. trials.
"I wanted a good start and a good race and I got both," the double Olympic silver medallist said.
Igor Kovacs of Slovakia won the high hurdles with the third fastest time this year, 13.21 seconds.
Tony Jarrett, Britain's double world championship silver medallist, slipped out of the blocks and did not finish.
